Fatty acid synthesis requires transport of citrate
from mitochondria to cytosol.

sourceEvidence.quote:
Systemic 1° carnitine deficiency—no cellular
uptake of carnitine → no transport of LCFAs
into mitochondria → toxic accumulation
of LCFAs in the cytosol.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.quote:
Causes weakness,
hypotonia, hypoketotic hypoglycemia, dilated
cardiomyopathy.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.quote:
Medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase
deficiency—↓ ability to break down fatty
acids into acetyl-CoA → accumulation of fatty
acyl carnitines and dicarboxylic acids in the
blood with hypoketotic hypoglycemia.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.quote:
Causes
vomiting, lethargy, seizures, coma, liver
dysfunction, hyperammonemia.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.quote:
Can lead to
sudden death in infants or children. Treat by
avoiding fasting.
